findings.description: SWR-DIA-001 requires each fault report within 10 ms. DEC-SWC-014 and OP-SWC-013 identify a four-report burst behind an answer line for which the fourth report can take up to 12.9 ms.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the report deadline and answer-line conflict, then specify and justify a mechanism that meets the resulting requirements.

findings.description: SWR-FLW-001 requires the flow check at the end of the release cycle, but T_DIAG can execute for 20 ms and may still be within its limit when its checkpoint is checked at the end of the 10 ms cycle.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the treatment of an unfinished T_DIAG and align the flow sequence and timing requirements with that decision.

findings.description: DEC-SWC-016 explicitly states that the CRC throughput and instruction counts underlying the execution allocations have not been established. The 500 µs segment and 10% processor targets therefore remain unsubstantiated.
findings.requested_change: Establish the platform clock and demonstrate the allocated execution times, including the CRC segment and remaining supervisor work, at that configuration.

findings.description: The revised 1 ms diagnostic response calculation counts control-cycle part B and timer events, but omits the 100 µs higher-priority part A. A response window can cross a cycle tick after part B, so the stated 760 µs interference bound is not justified.
findings.requested_change: Bound all higher-priority work that can occur in the response interval, including both control-cycle parts and timer events, and revise the report and answer timing analysis accordingly.

findings.description: DEC-SWC-017 allocates 85 µs for the last coincident compare decision, including 5 µs for each further decision. These allocations and the 10 µs timer unit are not yet established at the target configuration; OP-SWC-012 and OP-SWC-014 leave the necessary clock and timer feasibility unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Establish the timer resolution and demonstrate the complete coincident-event response bound at the chosen configuration.
